title: Working Set and WiredTiger Cache
content: The working set is the part of the data and indexes that is actively read or written, not the total data on disk. MongoDB's WiredTiger storage engine keeps recently used pages in its internal cache, which by default is the larger of 50% of (RAM minus 1 GB) or 256 MB. serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache reports bytes currently in the cache and maximum bytes configured, so cache usage percent is bytes in cache divided by the maximum. Pages read into cache counts pages that had to be loaded from disk; pages requested from the cache counts all page requests, so one minus pages read divided by pages requested approximates the cache hit ratio. When the working set no longer fits, pages read into cache and eviction pages evicted by application threads rise together, application threads spend time evicting, and queries that touch cold ranges become slower than queries on recently written data. Fixes are adding RAM or cache, adding indexes so queries touch fewer pages, archiving cold data, or sharding to spread the working set. Dirty bytes are modified pages not yet written to disk by a checkpoint; a high dirty share means writes are outpacing checkpoints.

title: Document Size and the 16 MB Limit
content: A single BSON document cannot exceed 16 MB. The $bsonSize aggregation operator returns the size in bytes of a document, for example {$bsonSize: '$$ROOT'}, which turns the embed versus reference decision into a measurement. Embedding comments inside a blog post is fast to read because one query returns everything, but the document grows with every comment, so a popular post with an unbounded comments array will eventually approach the 16 MB limit, and large documents also waste cache and network because the whole document is read even when only a few comments are shown. The rule of thumb from the lab is: fewer than about 100 comments per post, embed; more than 100, reference comments in their own collection; more than 1,000, use a paginated reference or bucket pattern that stores comments in fixed-size bucket documents. Bounded arrays such as a user's three shipping addresses are safe to embed. A capped array maintained with $push, $each and $slice keeps an embedded list bounded, which is how a chat application can keep the most recent messages inside a session document safely.

title: Monitoring MongoDB with serverStatus
content: The serverStatus command is the main source of runtime metrics. connections.current and connections.available show how close the server is to its connection limit; a common alert fires when current connections exceed 80% of the total. opcounters count inserts, queries, updates, deletes, getmores and commands since startup, so operations per second are computed from the difference between two samples divided by the time between them. wiredTiger.cache shows memory use and eviction pressure; an alert when cache usage exceeds 80% is the default threshold in the chapter 14 monitoring lab. mem.resident is the resident memory of the mongod process in megabytes, and network.bytesIn and bytesOut show traffic. For replica sets, replSetGetStatus reports each member's state and optime; replication lag is the difference between the primary's optimeDate and a secondary's optimeDate, and lag of more than about 10 seconds deserves an alert. Metrics should be logged over time, for example into a collection or a log file, so trends and spikes can be compared rather than judged from a single reading.
